conceptual_explanation: A 'Nominal Clause' is a whole clause that works like a single noun. It can be the subject of a sentence or the object of a verb. Using words like 'that', 'whether', and 'what' to start these clauses makes your writing much more sophisticated.

rule_cards.name: The 'That' Clause
rule_cards.correct: I believe that education is important.
rule_cards.incorrect: I believe education is important. (Less formal)

rule_cards.name: Whether/If Clauses
rule_cards.correct: I wonder whether the plan will work.
rule_cards.incorrect: I wonder the plan will work.

rule_cards.name: Question Word Clauses
rule_cards.correct: She explained how the system works.
rule_cards.incorrect: She explained how does the system work.

rule_cards.name: Subject Clauses
rule_cards.correct: That he passed the exam is a miracle.
rule_cards.incorrect: He passed the exam is a miracle.

head_noun_tasks.explanation: The nominal clause 'that technology can improve our lives' is the object of 'believe'.
The clause 'Whether we succeed or not' acts as the subject of the sentence.
The nominal clause 'where the nearest station was' is the object of 'asked'.
'That she is only ten years old' is a nominal clause acting as the subject.
The clause 'how to solve the complex equation' is the nominal object.

drill_tasks.question: ________ he said was not true.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'What' acts as the subject of the clause and the whole clause 'What he said' is the subject of the sentence.

drill_tasks.question: I don't know ________ the package will arrive today.
drill_tasks.explanation: In informal English 'if' is okay, but 'whether' is more formal for objects.

drill_tasks.question: Can you explain ________ you fixed the computer?
drill_tasks.explanation: Nominal clauses use statement word order (Subject + Verb), not question order.

drill_tasks.question: ________ the earth is round is a well-known fact.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'That' introduces a noun clause that functions as the subject.

drill_tasks.question: I am not sure ________ he is coming to the party.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'Whether' is used to express doubt or uncertainty.

boss_fight.paragraph: He passed the test is a surprise. I want to know where is the park. That he is late, it makes me angry.

errors.correction: That he passed the test is
errors.explanation: You need 'That' to turn a sentence into a noun clause that can act as a subject.
Inside a nominal clause, use statement order (Subject + Verb), not question order.

errors.original: That he is late, it makes
errors.explanation: The whole clause 'That he is late' is already the subject. Don't add an extra 'it'.

success_feedback: Great start! You've mastered the basics of turning whole ideas into nouns. This is a big step toward elite writing.
suggested_next_steps: Try Level 5 for more complex nominal structures!
